events.title: U.S. Constitution Takes Effect
events.description: The First Congress of the United States met in New York City and declared the new Constitution to be in operation, officially beginning government under the Constitution, although a quorum was not reached until later in the spring.
events.significance: Marked the formal start of the federal government under the U.S. Constitution, which remains the foundation of American governance.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Inaugurated as 16th U.S. President
events.description: Abraham Lincoln was sworn in as President amid the secession of seven Southern states. In his first inaugural address he appealed to national unity, declaring 'We are not enemies, but friends,' while asserting that the Union was perpetual.
events.significance: Lincoln's presidency guided the United States through the Civil War, preserved the Union, and led to the abolition of slavery.

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt Inaugurated; Frances Perkins Becomes First Female Cabinet Member
events.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt took office as the 32nd U.S. President during the depths of the Great Depression, declaring that 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.' Frances Perkins was named Secretary of Labor, becoming the first woman in a U.S. cabinet.
events.significance: Launched the New Deal era, which dramatically expanded the role of the federal government in the economy and social welfare, and broke a barrier for women in government.

events.title: Rutherford B. Hayes Inaugurated After Disputed Election
events.description: Rutherford B. Hayes was publicly sworn in as the 19th U.S. President after the contested 1876 election was resolved by the Compromise of 1877, following a private oath on March 3.
events.significance: The compromise led to the withdrawal of federal troops from the South, ending Reconstruction and ushering in the Jim Crow era.

events.title: Birth of the Modern Era of Vietnam War Era Context: Not Applicable
events.description: On March 4, 1681, King Charles II of England granted a royal charter to William Penn for the territory that became Pennsylvania, in repayment of a debt owed to Penn's father.
events.significance: The charter led to the founding of Pennsylvania, a colony based on religious tolerance and representative government that influenced American democratic ideals.
